Verification and validation status¶

Scientific software needs a distinction between verification (the equations were implemented as intended) and validation (the model predicts observations in its intended domain). Most of this repository’s evidence is currently verification. The simulator has not yet been calibrated end-to-end against a specific GNSS-R instrument or a collocated truth dataset.

Evidence levels used here¶

The documentation uses the following terms deliberately:

  1. Analytic verification – a closed-form identity, constraint, symmetry or limiting case is checked.

  2. Numerical verification – an analytic derivative or solver is compared with finite differences or a tighter independent residual.

  3. Regression protection – a golden file or fixed expected value detects unintended code changes.

  4. Plausibility check – a result lies in a deliberately broad physical envelope or follows an expected trend.

  5. External validation – predictions are compared with independent, polarisation- and geometry-matched observations with stated uncertainty.

Levels 1–4 exist in the test suite. Level 5 is still required before claiming absolute ocean NRCS, ship RCS, received power or detection probability.

Current evidence by subsystem¶

Subsystem

Evidence in the repository

Scientific interpretation

Sphere and WGS-84 specular geometry

Surface constraint, equal-angle residual, collinear case, analytic spherical occultation, and sphere/ellipsoid comparison.

Strong equation-level verification for tested geometries; no independent flight geolocation comparison.

Backscatter reflection point

Line/surface constraint, root beyond the receiver, sphere/ellipsoid selection and incidence gate.

Strong geometric verification of the defined collinear BRP model.

Delay-Doppler Jacobian

Finite-difference checks, including rigid Earth rotation; scaling and degeneracy tests.

Verified first-order local map away from singular points. Exact specular cells need second-order delay curvature and are not implemented.

Seawater permittivity and Fresnel terms

Closed-form limits, passivity and representative L-band regression values.

Equation/trend verification; not a fresh reproduction of the source datasets.

Cox-Munk, Elfouhaily and Bragg/two-scale ocean terms

PDF normalisation, positivity, wind/incidence trends, anisotropy and broad NRCS envelopes.

Plausibility plus regression protection. No polarisation-matched collocated measurement validation.

Bistatic link equation and thermal noise

Algebraic scaling, \(kTB\), \(C/N_0\), EIRP deltas and golden regression.

Link-equation implementation is verified; the input EIRP, antenna and target models control absolute accuracy.

Antenna

Array-factor peaks, steering convention, interpolation, input guards and golden regression.

Verified ideal isotropic-element array factor; not an efficiency-, coupling- or chamber-calibrated antenna model.

Ship RCS

Plate/dihedral formula peaks, nulls, visibility and component summation.

Internal formula verification only. Absolute ship RCS is preliminary.

Moving-target decision metric

Event plumbing and deterministic SCR/SINR/shadow calculations.

A screening metric, not a validated detector: no false-alarm probability, speckle distribution or delay-Doppler target-bin association.

Coverage

Grid construction, contiguous-track segmentation and cell intersection.

Verified pass-count algorithm. It is geometric coverage, not detection coverage.

Important interpretation rules¶

  • A passing golden-file test means the implementation did not change; it does not prove the frozen value is physically correct.

  • A broad dB envelope catches unit/sign failures but is not a curve-to-data validation.

  • noise_power_effective_w is a threshold-equivalent sensitivity scale. Incoherent averaging reduces estimator variance, not mean thermal noise power.

  • With delay_doppler_cell_enabled, the code changes the assumed ocean clutter area. It does not prove that a ship anywhere in the antenna footprint occupies the reference point’s delay-Doppler bin.

  • At the exact specular point the first-order delay gradient vanishes, so the implemented DDM area uses the antenna-footprint cap.

Minimum external-validation programme¶

Before using the model for absolute performance claims:

  1. Reproduce published Klein-Swift, Cox-Munk and Elfouhaily curves from digitised/reference data with explicit units, polarisation conventions and tolerances.

  2. Compare ocean NRCS or DDM slices against a mission product for matched carrier, incidence, wind speed, wind direction, wave age and antenna response.

  3. Replace fixed constellation/band EIRP assumptions with signal- and transmitter-specific values and propagate their uncertainty.

  4. Validate the antenna model against an element pattern or measured full-array pattern including efficiency, backlobe and scan loss.

  5. Compare the ship model with full-wave simulation, a defensible RCS database or measurements over aspect, polarisation and sea state.

  6. Implement target delay/Doppler coordinates, bin membership, speckle/noise statistics and a detector with specified probability of false alarm; then report probability of detection rather than only a deterministic threshold crossing.

  7. Record orbit/TLE epoch and IERS data versions for every geolocation comparison.

References¶

  • Klein, L. & Swift, C., IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation 25(1), 1977.

  • Cox, C. & Munk, W., Journal of the Optical Society of America 44(11), 1954.

  • Elfouhaily, T. et al., Journal of Geophysical Research 102(C7), 1997.

  • Zavorotny, V. & Voronovich, A., IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 38(2), 2000.

  • Vallado, D. A., Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications, 4th ed., 2013.
